bearings.paper_claim: Independent cascade extended to two colours. Each edge gets its activation coin and an exponential delay fixed before the run. Lemma 1 builds a deterministic equivalent in which each edge outcome is fixed in advance and a node takes the colour of the path that reaches it. The paper's random tie-breaking applies only when several players select the same seed node, not to simultaneous arrivals.
bearings.paper_location: Section 2 model (text lines 63-85); Section 3 Lemma 1 proof (lines 92-120)
bearings.system_side: Edge draws are keyed by iteration, u and v with no colour in the key, so one draw per edge serves whichever colour reaches it, and a coloured node is never recoloured. This matches the fixed-in-advance edge equivalence. The code drops the exponential delays and runs hop-synchronous spread. B is anti-tier members plus neutral bystanders drawn with probability min(0.9, industry dollars/400000); the code matches this.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Edge-level CRN and first-colour-wins carry over. Timing does not: unit hops replace the paper's continuous delays, so the paper's equivalence does not cover the system's timing. The bystander mapping (0.9 cap, 400000 scale) and the kernel constant 6 have no basis in the paper.
bearings.verifier_note: The rel paper_claim misattributes random tie-breaking to simultaneous arrivals. The paper uses continuous delays to avoid arrival ties and randomizes only between players who pick the same seed. The code structure matches the paper's edge equivalence; the hop timing is a departure.

bearings.paper_claim: The paper avoids ties between simultaneous activation attempts by giving each attempt a continuous exponential delay. It randomizes only between players who select the same seed node. The rel claim that simultaneous arrivals are tie-broken at random is not in the text.
bearings.paper_location: Section 2 (text lines 63-85), the sentence beginning 'To avoid tie-breaking for simultaneous activation attempts'
bearings.system_side: The cascade is hop-synchronous. The frontier is built A-first and children are appended in processing order, so by induction every A node in a layer is processed before any B node. A node reached in the same hop by both colours goes to A. Same-hop ties are therefore resolved deterministically in A's favour.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The departure from the paper's no-tie design is confirmed by reading the code. Its effect on CU reach is unmeasured. A rerun with B-first or randomized frontier order under the same draws would measure it. Remains UNVERIFIED under DE-062.
bearings.verifier_note: The departure is real but the paper citation is wrong. Reword as a departure from the paper's stated no-tie design. The size of the bias is not established.

bearings.paper_claim: Lemma 1 gives monotone submodularity of a player's expected reach in its own seeds, holding the other players' seed sets fixed. Greedy over that function gives a (1-1/e) approximation to the best response (Theorem 1).
bearings.paper_location: Section 3, Lemma 1 and Theorem 1 (text lines 92-120); abstract lines 13-16
bearings.system_side: Lazy greedy with MAXSEEDS 60 ranks each candidate by max(0, spread gain) times fac. fac is leverage, or the competitiveness multiplier if the LEV source is set to it, and REPFAC times leverage for contest plays. Seeds are gated at random. Contest plays remove B seeds. The bystander set excludes any node already in the A seed set, so the opponent set changes with S, which Lemma 1 does not cover.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The raw-spread guarantee applies only with a fixed opponent set and A-seed additions. Independent per-seed gating is an expectation over independent masks and keeps submodularity. The fac-weighted ranking is a heuristic, not greedy on spread. Contest removal and the S-dependent bystander exclusion fall outside Lemma 1. MC of 20 adds noise. The bound holds only with fac equal to 1, which is the LEV-off case.
bearings.verifier_note: The qualifies relation is right. The rel missed the S-dependent bystander exclusion. The docstring at scenario.py 9-12 states the (1-1/e) claim for the coalition side, and the guarantee must be narrowed as the rel says. The COMPET_MULT to LEV source link was not checked.

bearings.paper_claim: Reach is submodular in a player's own seeds, so summed single-seed marginals overstate the joint gain; the (1-1/e) guarantee belongs to greedy, not to individual marginals (Lemma 1, Theorem 1).
bearings.system_side: The allocator computes single-seed marginals against the base, multiplies each by (1 + 0.8 times bpf), water-fills 2,000,000 dollars with a 50,000 per-member cap in proportion to those boosted values, runs no greedy, and reports the joint spread of the funded set. The code comment cites submodularity for that report.
bearings.code_ref: fec/engine/per_topic_coalition.py:6 (BUDGET, CAP); fec/engine/per_topic_coalition.py:30-135 (BETA_C, coal_waterfill, allocation loop)
bearings.transfer_conditions: Submodularity implies the joint report is at most the naive additive sum, so the joint report is supported as inference. The paper gives no guarantee for a proportional water-fill. The bystander set excludes funded seeds, so the spread is not Lemma 1's fixed-opponent function. The figures are one allocation run per topic at MC 20.
bearings.verifier_note: The rel says the split is proportional to single-seed marginals; the code uses marginals boosted by (1 + 0.8 bpf). The no-greedy and joint-report claims check out. The code's submodularity premise carries the same bystander caveat.

bearings.paper_claim: The best-response guarantee holds only for the last committer. Pure Nash equilibria need not exist and mixed ones do (lines 83-85). Theorem 2 bounds the price of competition at 2 on total activations, not on any one player's share. First-mover results cover only a duopoly on disjoint lines (Lemma 2, lines 149-153).
bearings.paper_location: Section 2 lines 83-85; Section 3 Theorem 2 lines 121-128; Section 4 Lemma 2 lines 149-153
bearings.system_side: Scenarios hold industry fixed. Competitor money enters only as exogenous bystander probabilities (industry dollars over 400000, capped at 0.9) and as the comp leg of money_response, which was not opened. Industry never re-optimizes against CU's seeds. The scenario docstring limits the (1-1/e) claim to a follower facing a fixed opponent.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The fixed-opponent framing holds only if industry commits first and never reacts. FEC filings are public, so if industry reacts, CU becomes a first mover on a general graph, where the paper gives no algorithm or guarantee. The price-of-competition bound says nothing about CU's own share.
bearings.verifier_note: The paper claims check out and the docstring limits match the paper. The comp leg in money_response was not checked, so the claim is reproduced for the bystander channel only.

summary_issues: Overall verdict: softened, not refuted. The code-structure claims check out against the text and code. The summary misstates the paper's tie-breaking and overstates the Paul-alignment and lines-only claims.
Summary says simultaneous arrivals are broken at random. The paper uses continuous exponential delays to avoid arrival ties and randomizes only between players who select the same seed (Section 2).

Summary says guarantees exist only for lines once the rival best-responds. The paper gives first-mover algorithms only for a duopoly on disjoint lines and no guarantee on general graphs. Reword accordingly.

Summary says the system cites the paper's submodularity result to justify lazy greedy. Only the scenario docstring (9-12) and the per_topic_coalition comment were found citing it. No lazy-greedy citation was located, so that part is unsupported.
Summary and bearing 4 say the water-fill is proportional to single-seed marginals. The code uses marginals boosted by (1 + 0.8 bpf). Correct the wording.

paul_alignment cites a Chen 2023 note on submodularity failing under linear-threshold contagion. The Chen item is dated 2021 and is a contingency-aware RL influence-maximization paper, not a linear-threshold paper. The 'not diminishing' phrase was not found in the Chen item. Unsupported as written.

paul_alignment cites Paul's margin note on Kim et al. 2025 and a Fink note. The item paul_entries array is empty, the ext paul_markup array is empty, and no matching note was located elsewhere in the research items. Cannot verify; remove or source.
paul_alignment says the built Monte Carlo is a faithful live-edge implementation. Only the edge draws are faithful. The timing and bystander exclusions are departures (see bearings 1-3).
